newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-STEELERS BEAT DOLPHINS IN MIAMI.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-STEELERS BEAT DOLPHINS IN MIAMI.

text.p: Mike Tomczak's 20-yard touchdown pass to Ernie Mills with 2:10 remaining lifted the Pittsburgh Steelers to a 24-17 victory over the Miami Dolphins Monday.

With just over six minutes remaining in regulation Tomczak moved the Steelers 45 yards in eight plays. After backup quarterback and utility man Kordell Stewart kept the drive alive with a key run for a first down, Tomczak threw a bullet to Mills, who caught his first touchdown pass of the season.
"This is a big victory," Tomczak said.
"We came together as a group tonight and hopefully set the time for the balance of the season."
After Mills's touchdown, Dan Marino drove Miami down to the Pittsburgh 7-yard line but Scott Miller couldn't haul in Marino's pass in the end zone on 4th-and-1.
"Dan Marino is a great football player on a very good football team," Pittsburgh coach Bill Cowher said. "Nothing is safe when he has the football at the end of a game in a crucial situation."
The Steelers improved to 10-1 on Monday nights under Cowher. The only setback came at Miami, in 1995.

Tomczak completed 16-of-29 passes for 252 yards as Pittsburgh (9-3) won for the fourth time in its last five games. Jerome Bettis carried 27 times for 119 yards, recording his ninth 100-yard game of the season.

Miami (6-6) has lost four of its last six games and is in danger of missing the playoffs for the first time since 1993. The Dolphins are tied with Indianapolis for third place in the AFC East, two games behind New England and three in back of Buffalo.
Miami was penalised nine times for 54 yards.

"This is a frustrating loss," said Miami coach Jimmy Johnson. "I felt like, and the players felt like, we could win this ballgame. We had plenty of opportunities to win the ballgame but we didn't make the plays when we needed to. We got too many penalties and the opponent only had one penalty. You cannot expect to win games that way."
"It's a very difficult loss because I felt we should have won," Marino said. "We had some penalties that hurt us but you have to overcome them."
Marino, who was 22-of-37 for 254 yards, tossed a two-yard pass to O.J. McDuffie to cap a 15-play, 76-yard drive and give the Dolphins a 7-0 lead with 5:15 left in the first quarter.
Norm Johnson kicked a 47-yard field goal as Pittsburgh cut the deficit to 7-3 with 2:15 left in the first.
Calvin Jackson picked off a pass from Tomczak and returned it 61 yards to give the Dolphins a 14-3 advantage, 7:12 into the second quarter.
Tim Lester had a five-yard run as the Steelers closed within 14-10 with 3:30 left in the first half. Stewart kept an 8-play, 80-yard drive going with a one-yard run to the Miami 5 on 4th-and-1.
"I told our club at halftime after the drive in which we scored a touchdown that made the score 14-10 that we were controlling the game," Cowher said.

In the third quarter, the versatile Stewart was used at quarterback again at the end of a 12-play, 82-yard drive and produced a one-yard burst to give the Steelers a 17-14 advantage seven minutes into the third quarter.
Miami tied the score, 17-17, on Joe Nedney's 42-yard field goal with 2:34 left in the third.
